hook_line: Tokyo has more Michelin stars than any city on Earth, and some of its best food is still served at a counter for pocket change.
intro: Tokyo has more Michelin stars than any city on Earth, and some of its best food is still served at a counter for pocket change.
facts: Cross Shibuya Crossing at rush hour, when up to 3,000 people cross at once, then watch it again from a cafe window above.
Wake up early for Senso-ji in Asakusa, Tokyo's oldest temple, and walk the lantern-lined street before the crowds and incense arrive.
Eat where locals eat: counter ramen or standing sushi in the Tsukiji outer market costs a fraction of any fine-dining set menu.
For the view, skip the ticket queues at Skytree and ride up the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, where the observation deck needs no ticket.
At night squeeze into a six-seat bar in Golden Gai or Omoide Yokocho, where yakitori smoke fills alleys barely wide enough to walk.
outro: Save this for your Tokyo trip.
